phase0_ownership_inventory.why_standalone_never_reached_it: GemmaDenseStage._setup_context builds the same HybridSWAKVCache pool directly via create_kvcache_pool with a fixed identity page table (page_table[i] == i) and NO CacheManager: no code path between _setup_context and the attention backend ever calls alloc_swa, so full_to_swa_index_mapping remained the all-zero init sentinel for the process lifetime. Every SWA-layer store wrote swa slot 0 (racing warps -> varying bytes) and every prefix gather read slot 0 (#157: chunk-2 nondeterminism, earliest varying boundary L0_kv_slice_post_write).
phase0_ownership_inventory.session_state_owner_in_standalone_path: GemmaDenseStage itself: single request at a time, ctx.page_table a fixed identity row, reset_session_state() between sessions (drivers: stage_chain RESET op per generate(), single_gpu_control per step, last_stage_service per session, two_stage, #157 replay harness, #97/#110 services).

mapping_validity_timeline.creation: pool __init__/_init_swa_paged_state builds sentinel mapping + full free-list
mapping_validity_timeline.first_prefill: must be valid for [0, chunk_rows) BEFORE prepare_metadata translates the page-table range (the first prefix-consuming SWA operation)
mapping_validity_timeline.extend_prefill: must be valid for [0, start+rows) before the chunk's gathers/stores
mapping_validity_timeline.decode: must be valid for [0, position+1] before the step
mapping_validity_timeline.reset_reuse: all ownership released (mapping all-sentinel, free-list whole) — never inherited
mapping_validity_timeline.teardown_abort: process teardown drops the pool (CUDA context destruction); abort within a session leaves the frontier observable; next session's reset releases everything
mapping_validity_timeline.exhaustion: RuntimeError (fail-closed) — never continues on sentinel slot 0

phase0_ownership_inventory.allocation_failure_behavior: alloc_swa raises RuntimeError('SWA pool exhausted') when the free-list is shorter than the request; the #166 lifecycle checks swa_available_size() first and raises a named fail-closed error before consuming anything (no partial allocation: the frontier is advanced only after a successful alloc_swa).
phase0_ownership_inventory.chosen_owner: GemmaDenseStage (the standalone stage runtime), via a session-ownership lifecycle at the same lifecycle points the scheduler uses.
rejected_alternatives: Pasting the #157 diagnostic intervention (alloc_swa over arange(used) after each reset) at driver call sites: rejected — drivers are many (chain/single/control/diagnostic/#97/#110 services), the seam would be duplicated per driver, and the allocation would sit AFTER reset but have no persistence/failure contract of its own.

Allocating inside prepare_metadata / the attention backend: rejected — the backend is a generic pool consumer; giving it allocator authority inverts the scheduler's ownership model and would change every non-standalone path.

Building a CacheManager instance inside the stage runtime: rejected — the standalone path has no page-allocator role (page table is a fixed identity), so the manager would be dead weight plus a second ownership authority.
Modifying HybridSWAKVCache to self-allocate on store_kv: rejected — silently allocates behind the scheduler's back on the shared-pool path (double allocation), violating exactly-once ownership.

remediation_design.owner_seam: GemmaDenseStage._ensure_swa_session_mapping / _reset_swa_session_ownership / _swa_pool / swa_session_ownership_report, wired into all four execution branches (prefill first/single + receiver, decode first/single + receiver) BEFORE self._prepare.
remediation_design.mechanism: incremental ownership frontier [0, allocated): each call allocates exactly the not-yet-owned positions of the upcoming chunk's full referenced range (chunk rows + prefix gathers), via pool.alloc_swa over arange(frontier, need_end) — the SAME underlying allocation semantic as CacheManager.allocate_paged per chunk and as the accepted #157 one-variable intervention.
remediation_design.reset_ordering: reset_session_state zeroes pool tensors THEN rebuilds the allocator via _init_swa_paged_state — the zero loop also zeroes _swa_free (a top-level pool tensor), and a zeroed free-list would hand out reserved sentinel slot 0 on the next alloc_swa (the #157-recorded trap); rebuilding after the zeroes guarantees the pristine __init__ ownership state.
remediation_design.pool_sizing: num_swa_tokens = max_seq_len + 1 (sentinel convention, matching rebuild_from_config's num_pages+1) so a full-capacity session is not one slot short.
remediation_design.non_swa: getattr(pool, 'swa_paged', False) gate — non-SWA pools never enter the lifecycle (no unnecessary SWA state).
